title: Residue identifications of powered parameter quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a commutative $k$-algebra, $d,c\in\mathbb N$, $c\ge1$, $P=k[X_i\mid i\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]$, $\varphi:P\to\Lambda$ a $k$-algebra map, and $q\subset\Lambda$ a prime. Suppose the images of $\varphi(X_i)$ generate the maximal ideal of $\Lambda_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Put $J=((X_i^c)^8)$, $J_\Lambda=J\Lambda$. For every prime $q_0\subset\Lambda/J_\Lambda$ contracting to $q$, put $p_0=q_0\cap(P/J)$, $R_0=(P/J)_{p_0}$, $L_0=(\Lambda/J_\Lambda)_{q_0}$, $L=\operatorname{ULift}(L_0)$, and $I=\mathfrak m_{R_0}$. There exist ring isomorphisms $e_R:R_0/I\simeq k$ and $e_L:L/IL\simeq\kappa(q)$ such that $e_L(r\cdot1)=\operatorname{algebraMap}_{k,\kappa(q)}(e_R(r))$ for every $r\in R_0/I$. No regularity, dimension or separability hypothesis is required.

source.place: Lemma 07FE (lemma-resolve-special), proof, final paragraph: flat local parameter quotients and their separable residue extension

proof.text: In P/J every X_i has its c-th power raised to the eighth equal to zero. Since p₀ is prime, each X_i lies in p₀. For the composite k-algebra map P → (P/J)/p₀, polynomial induction (constants, sums, products with a variable) shows every image is a constant. The two quotient maps are surjective, so k → (P/J)/p₀ is surjective. It is injective because k is a field and the quotient by a prime is nontrivial.

The resulting ring equivalence k ≃ (P/J)/p₀ makes p₀ maximal. Mathlib Ideal.bijective_algebraMap_quotient_residueField then identifies (P/J)/p₀ with its residue field R₀/I. Compose the two surjective algebra maps and invert AlgEquiv.ofBijective to obtain the k-algebra equivalence eR: R₀/I ≃ k.

The contraction equality q = comap(q₀) gives the local ring map f: Λ_q → L₀. It is surjective by localization of the quotient map, implemented directly by RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_surjective and localRingHom_surjective. Thus map f of the maximal ideal of Λ_q equals the maximal ideal of L₀. Each variable lies in p₀, so its image in R₀ lies in I. The quotient square and scalar towers identify its image in L₀ with f(φ(X_i)/1). Mapping the generating span hgen therefore shows m(L₀) ≤ IL₀; locality of R₀ → L₀ gives the reverse inclusion.

The quotient map Λ → Λ/JΛ induces a bijective canonical k-algebra map κ(q) → κ(q₀): the local map f is surjective, and the induced residue map is injective because its source is a field. Use Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ and RingHom.SurjectiveOnStalks.residueFieldMap_bijective to obtain eQ. ULift.down carries IL to m(L₀), by map_map and the previous ideal equality. Ideal.quotientEquivAlg gives L/IL ≃ₐ[k] κ(q₀); composing with eQ inverse gives eL.

For any r in R₀/I, surjectivity of k → R₀/I writes r as the class of a scalar a. The induced map on quotients sends it to the class of algebraMap R₀ L (algebraMap k R₀ a), which equals the class of algebraMap k L a by the scalar-tower equality. Both eR and eL are k-algebra equivalences, so their commutes equations give eL(r·1) = algebraMap k κ(q)(eR(r)). Polynomial induction and span arguments also cover the empty variable set.

lean.statement:
theorem parameter_quotient_residue_ringEquivs
    {k : Type u} {Λ : Type w} [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    (d c : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum Λ)
    (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d ↦
      algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) (φ (MvPolynomial.X i)))) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)) :
    letI := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    let J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) :=
      Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin d ↦ (MvPolynomial.X i ^ c) ^ 8))
    let J_Λ := Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) Λ) J
    ∀ (q₀ : PrimeSpectrum (Λ ⧸ J_Λ)),
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk J_Λ) q₀ = q →
    letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver
      (q₀.asIdeal.under (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k ⧸ J)) q₀.asIdeal
    let R₀ := Localization.AtPrime (q₀.asIdeal.under (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k ⧸ J))
    let L₀ := Localization.AtPrime q₀.asIdeal
    let L := ULift.{max u v} L₀
    let I := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀
    ∃ eR : (R₀ ⧸ I) ≃+* k,
      ∃ eL : (L ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R₀ L)) ≃+* q.asIdeal.ResidueField,
        ∀ r : R₀ ⧸ I,
          eL (algebraMap (R₀ ⧸ I) (L ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R₀ L)) r) =
            algebraMap k q.asIdeal.ResidueField (eR r)
